title: Reception look jewellery: switching from traditional to glam
description: Switching from a traditional wedding look to a glam reception? What jewellery to remove, what to keep and how to restyle fast for a gown, saree or lehenga.
intro: The easiest way to make your reception look feel different from the wedding is to change three things: the metal or stone style, the number of pieces, and where the focus sits. Most brides move from layered gold Kundan to one sleek American Diamond or polki-look set, take off the head and nose jewellery, and let the earrings and necklace do all the work.

sections.heading: Decide what kind of reception look you want
paragraphs: Receptions vary widely. Some are cocktail-style evenings with gowns and music, some are formal dinners where the couple greets hundreds of guests, and some happen on the same night as the wedding with only an hour to change. Before you plan jewellery, be clear about the outfit and the time you will have.

A gown or Indo-western drape calls for a properly modern look. A heavy saree or second lehenga can stay semi-traditional but lighter than the wedding. Knowing which you are going for keeps you from wearing a half-wedding, half-party look that does not quite land.

sections.heading: What to take off
paragraphs: Removing pieces is the fastest way to change the mood. These are the usual candidates:
list: Maang tikka, mathapatti or passa, especially if your hair is being let down or restyled.
Nath, which is strongly associated with the wedding ceremony itself.
The long rani haar, if you wore a choker and haar together.
Haathphool and extra bangles, keeping only what tradition asks you to keep.
Kamarbandh, unless you are wearing a saree that needs it.

sections.heading: What you may want to keep
paragraphs: Some pieces carry meaning beyond the look. Many brides keep their chooda, bangles, mangalsutra or sindoor through the reception, and families can have firm views on this. Check in advance rather than on the night.

If you are keeping a red chooda or gold bangles, choose reception jewellery that sits comfortably with them. A gold-toned American Diamond set or polki-look set links more easily to a red chooda than a stark silver set does. If you are wearing a gown, a slim mangalsutra can sit under or alongside a short necklace without fuss.

sections.heading: Matching jewellery to the reception outfit
paragraphs: For a gown, go for a single statement necklace, often a sparkling AD choker or a fine collar piece, with matching drop earrings. Keep the wrist simple with one bracelet or a dressy watch. Our [Heritage collection](/heritage) includes AD and Russian-stone sets that suit this kind of finish.

For a saree, a choker or short necklace with a longer set of earrings is classic. Drape matters: if the pallu is pinned neatly on the shoulder, the necklace stays fully visible; if it is draped loosely, a shorter piece sits better than a long one.

For a second lehenga, pick a set that contrasts with the wedding one. If your wedding set was gold Kundan with red and green, try silver-toned AD, or a polki-look set with white stones. The aim is for the reception photos to look like a fresh chapter.

sections.heading: Planning the quick change
paragraphs: When the reception follows the wedding on the same day, you may have under an hour. Make it easy on yourself.

Pack the reception jewellery in one labelled pouch, with earrings, necklace and any ring together. Give a trusted person a second empty pouch for everything you take off, so wedding pieces do not get lost in a crowded room. Ask your stylist to take off the head jewellery before restyling your hair, not after. Change earrings last, once the hair is done, so nothing gets tangled.
Keep a small mirror, safety pins and a spare pair of earring backs in the reception pouch as well, so small fixes do not hold up the change.

sections.heading: Hair, makeup and jewellery together
paragraphs: Reception looks often come with open hair, soft waves or a sleek low bun. Open hair partly hides earrings, so choose drops long enough to show below the hair line, or tuck one side behind the ear for photos. A sleek bun shows off everything and suits a bold choker.

Makeup usually shifts too, from a deep bridal lip to a nude, berry or glossy one. Silver and white-stone jewellery tends to look crisp with cooler, softer makeup, while gold-toned pieces suit warm, bronzed looks.

sections.heading: Finishing touches
paragraphs: A reception is mostly spent greeting guests and posing on stage, so you need somewhere to keep your phone, a lipstick, tissues and spare earring backs. A structured clutch or embellished potli completes the glam look in a way a plain bag cannot. Browse our [potli bags and Kundan clutches](/potli-bags) if you want one that matches the reception outfit.

faq.q: Should the reception jewellery be different from the wedding jewellery?
faq.a: Usually yes. A change in style, such as Kundan to American Diamond, makes the reception photos feel like a new look.

faq.q: What jewellery goes with a reception gown?
faq.a: One statement necklace with matching drop earrings and a simple bracelet or watch. Skip the tikka and nath.

faq.q: Can I wear my chooda with a reception gown?
faq.a: Many brides do. Choose gold-toned reception jewellery so it connects comfortably with the red of the chooda.

faq.q: How do I change jewellery quickly between wedding and reception?
faq.a: Pack reception pieces in one labelled pouch, remove head jewellery before hair restyling and put earrings on last.
